what: It is a Hong Kong contractor that does building repair, maintenance, renovation and painting work, mainly on public sector projects.
proceeds: It plans to use about 40% for buying or investing in building work firms and 30% for painting equipment and machinery. About 20% is for hiring skilled staff, and the rest is for general costs and working capital.
risks: US rules on auditors of emerging market companies are getting stricter, which could affect the company if its auditor is not inspected by US regulators.
Cash and assets held in Hong Kong may be blocked from use outside Hong Kong by government limits on transfers.
Court judgments that shareholders win against the company may not be enforceable.
Its management has no experience running a US public company or following the laws that apply to one.
As a holding company, it relies on dividends from its Hong Kong subsidiary to pay its own dividends.
